Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com. h DILG OPINION No. 42 s.E023 JUN 20 zoa ATTY. GERARDO M. LABASTILLA Provincial Legal Officer Province of Agusan Del Sur Dear Atty. Labastilla: This has reference to your letter dated April 26, 2023 requesting this Department's opinion on the request of a former Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member, Edwin Demegillo for the payment of his back salaries. The facts and circumstances of the case are as follows: A case was filed against Mr. Demegillo and other respondents before the Office of the Ombudsman for Conduct Prejudicial to the Best Interest of the Service and Grace Misconduct. In a Decision of the Ombudsman dated April 4, 2016, they were found guilty of the charge and dismissed from service. The subject Decision was implemented by this Department last October 20, 2016. Consequently, the case was appealed to the Court of Appeals (CA) where it thereafter reversed and set aside the Decision of the Ombudsman. The Motion for Reconsideration was denied by the CA, and Notice of Entry of Judgment certified that the Decision has become final and executory on January 25, 2018. The appellate court did not discuss the administrative findings of the Ombudsman as it was rendered nugatory by the blanket and wholesale absolution of the administrative charge and consequently dismissed due to the application of the condonation doctrine or the Aguinaldo Doctrine. Hence, this inquiry. Please be informed that the Department has previously tackled a similar case. The Department had on an occasion to opine the following to wit: In a letter dated 21 April 2017, the Office of the Ombudsman, through Assistant Ombudsman Asryman Rafanan, laid down the conditions necessary for the grant of back salaries in administrative disciplinary cases, thus: As held by the Court in the Civil Service Commission vs. Cruz, there are two conditions necessary for the grant of back salaries in administrative disciplinary cases, namely: (a) the employee must be found innocent of the charges; and (b) his suspension must be unjustified. Hence, back salaries shall be paid only if the government official or employee is completely exonerated of the charge against him Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

and his suspension or dismissal is found and declared to be unjustified. (emphasis supplied) Upon perusal of the reasons cited by the CA in its Amended Decision, we learned the following: (l ) The CA applied the recent case of Almario-TempIenuevo vs. Office of the Ombudsman, wherein the Supreme Court, on appeal, reversed the Court of Appeals and ruled that the condonation doctrine will apply despite its abandonment in the case of Carpio Morales vs. CA and even if it involved a public officer who was elected to a different position provided that it is shown that the body politic electing the person to another office if the same as held in the case of Giron vs. Ochoa; The CA found the condonation doctrine applicable in the case of (2) respondent Bonachita-RicabIanca following the Supreme Court's ruling in the Almario-TempIonuevo vs. Ombudsman case. When one is condoned like herein respondent Bonachita-RicabIanca, it does not mean that she was also found "innocent of the charges". These two terms are different from each other. The latter is one of the two (2) conditions in order for one to become entitled to back salaries. The term "innocent of the charges" requires that the respondent must not be found guilty (even the slightest wrongdoing) of the offense charged. "Condonation" or the Condonation Doctrine, on the other hand, implies that respondent should have been found guilty by the court of the offense charged but due to his re-election to office, there is an assumption that the electorate disregarded or forgave his fault or misconduct. It arises from the principle that it is not for the court, by reason of such fault or misconduct, to practically overrule the will of the people. It is apparent in the discussion of the CA in its Amended Decision that respondent Bonachita-RicabIanca should have been found guilty of the offense charged were it not for the timely issuance by the Supreme Court of its ruling in the Almario-Templenuevo applying the condonation doctrinel. Based on the foregoing, it is clear that acquittal or exoneration is different from condonation. Exoneration or acquittal requires that respondent official is found innocent of the charges2. Thus, Condonation or Aguinaldo Doctrine does not necessarily mean, just exoneration or acquittal, that the respondent elective official is not guilty of the charge. Respondent official might have been guilty of the charge, if the proceedings continued, only that, before the decision on the administrative case against him was rendered, he was reelected by his constituents and as such forgave his previous fault or misconduct3. In view thereof, we are of the view that the request of SP Demegillo has no leg to stand on. Correspondingly, we affirm the findings laid out in the draft response prepared by the Provincial Legal Office and recommend attaching a copy of this legal opinion as supporting document. 1 DILG Opinion No. 83 s.2019. 2 Plaza et. al. vs. CA, GR. 138464, January 18, 2008. 3 DILG Opinion No. 9, s. 2015. Page 2 of 3

Finally, this opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BYA ORITY OF THE SECR N OR R. LLAMAS ATTY nd ecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affai OU LA/JRL/LLLS-LRALLD1sb11clp copy furnished: DONAL D.
